name: Unit lifecycle
purpose: The unit's six statuses and the twelve transitions the S3 loop takes between them are one closed table, `UNIT_TRANSITIONS` in the protocol, and the execution store refuses a status change that is not a row of it. The table is what the figure of the lifecycle is drawn from and what a unit's history is replayed through: `unitTrajectory` (core) folds the attempt records, the verdicts, the recovery decisions and the obligations through the table in time order, gives each step its why as the records state it — the rule the router applied, the reasons the verdict carries, the obligation the unit waited on — and says when the fold and the record disagree. The control room's Lifecycle view steps through it.

absorbs.description: A unit marked closed by a hand edit, a test fixture or a branch of the loop nobody drew; a 'why did this unit stop?' answered by reading six logs by hand; a state diagram on the website the code had already outgrown.

enforcementPoints.note: ExecutionStore.setStatus: dispatch, dispatch-refused, attempt-failed, verified; the table is UNIT_TRANSITIONS in ../protocol/src/execution.ts
unitTrajectory (../core/src/trajectory.ts): the fold on every unit view, which the control room steps through

emits: a refusal on an undeclared status change
the unit's trajectory, in the status read model

cost.description: One table lookup per status change; one read of the unit's records per status view, which the read model makes anyway.

may: refuse a status change the table does not declare
replay the records through the table
say that the replay and the record disagree
mayNot: infer a status from the repository or the transcript
state a why the records do not carry

limitations: The gate is on the pair (from, to), not on the trigger: which row the loop took is read back from the records, not written down with the status. Three rows share blocked → blocked (a resumed dispatch refused, a re-audit refused, a waiting decision) and are told apart by the record beside them.

The store keeps only the current status, so the history is a reconstruction. Three moves leave no record of their own — reintegrated, reintegration refused, and a dispatch refused before any attempt — and the fold places them at the record that follows (the decision, or the unit record's last write). A status history in the store, one line per transition with its trigger, would make the fold a read; not yet (DEBT row 42).

The why is what the records say. A record that carries no rationale — an attempt that ended `error`, a verdict with no reasons — gives its step a detail string and nothing more; the fold does not read the transcript to improve on it.
A status written around the loop is caught only where the fold and the record disagree; a forged history that happens to be a path through the table is not.

ablation.note: A type and a store gate over the loop's own writes; switching it off changes no run the loop performs, only what a hand edit can do.

retirement.condition: Retire when the store writes the transition, with its trigger, instead of the status — the table as the store's own schema, with nothing left to replay.
